import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between price and megapixels, colored by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=cameras,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor=None
)

# Add title and labels
scatter_plot.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
scatter_plot.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
scatter_plot.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Adjust the legend
scatter_plot.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Save the plot as 'output.png'

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
cameras = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of seaborn
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between price and megapixels, colored by sensor type
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
scatter_plot = sns.scatterplot(
    data=cameras,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor=None
)

# Add title and labels
scatter_plot.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=16)
scatter_plot.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=14)
scatter_plot.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14)

# Adjust the legend
scatter_plot.legend(title='Sensor Type', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Save the plot as 'output.png'
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
